The facts of the case are, that the opposite-party No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 44 of 1991 against the present petitioners and opposite party No. 2 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act for recovery of Khas possession of the suit land described in the plaint stating, inter alia, that he purchased the suit land from the real owner by two registered sale deeds dated 25-7-1984 and 28-10-1981 respectively, and since purchase he has been possessing the same on payment of rent. Thereafter defendant Nos. 1 and 2 tried to dispossess him from the land and the plaintiff filed a Title Suit being No. 81 of 1990 praying for permanent injunction and got a decree against him. Subsequently while the plaintiff opposite-party was in possession of the land the defendant petitioners dispossessed him from the suit land on 4-12-1991 and then the plaintiff opposite party filed a suit being No. 100 of 1992 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act for recovery of khas possession of the suit land. The present petitioners contested the suit by filing a written statement stating, inter alia, that the plaintiffs are not the real owner of the suit land and that they never possessed the suit land. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing both the parties decreed the suit against the petitioners. Being aggrieved at this judgment and decree the petitioners preferred this petition under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. For the reasons stated above I maintained the impugned judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge for recovery of Khas possession of the land in suit.
